brief: How to protect 4 hours of deep work in a calendar full of meetings.

slots.headline: How to Protect Four Hours of Deep Work in a Meeting-Heavy Calendar

slots.title: Audit Your Calendar
slots.body: Scan your week and flag every recurring meeting that lacks a clear owner or agenda. Cancel or delegate anything that does not require your direct input. This single step often reveals two to three hours of hidden free time.

slots.title: Block Deep Work
slots.body: Treat your focus sessions like immovable client appointments. Reserve a consistent four-hour block each morning before Slack and email hijack your attention. Protect it ruthlessly.

slots.title: Defend the Buffer
slots.body: Never schedule meetings back-to-back. Insert a fifteen-minute buffer to reset your mind and capture action items. That small gap preserves mental clarity for deep work.

slots.title: Say No Politely
slots.body: Decline invites that do not align with your core priorities. Offer a brief explanation or suggest an async update instead. Your calendar reflects what you value most.

slots.title: Batch All Meetings
slots.body: Cluster calls into one or two dedicated afternoons rather than scattering them throughout the week. Batching minimizes context switching and leaves larger uninterrupted stretches for focused work.

slots.title: Close the Apps
slots.body: Silence notifications and exit email during your deep-work block. Even brief pings fracture concentration and extend task completion time. Guard your attention like a scarce resource.

slots.headline: Reclaim Four Hours Daily
slots.body: Start blocking deep work tomorrow and watch your output transform.
